subject: Basic Electricity
sourceFile: Technical & Trade -- APPLIED ELECTRICITY OR BASIC ELECTRICITY.txt
examFormat: Three papers, all compulsory; Papers 1 and 2 are taken at one sitting. Paper 1: fifty multiple-choice questions in 1 hour for 50 marks. Paper 2: Section A (compulsory, four questions, answer three) and Section C for Nigeria, Sierra Leone and The Gambia (three questions, answer two), five questions in all, 1 hour for 50 marks. Paper 3: practical paper of two experiments, both carried out, in 3 hours for 100 marks.
excluded: Section B (Ghana only): Topics 11-13 (Electron Emission, Semiconductor, Communication), because they are for Ghana candidates only.

subtopics.name: Structure of matter
objectives: Explain, qualitatively, the structure of atoms in relation to electric current

subtopics.name: Conductors and insulators
objectives: Define conductors and insulators and give examples and characteristics (qualitative treatment only)

subtopics.name: Resistors
objectives: Identify the types of resistors
Use the resistor colour code
Calculate resistors in series and parallel
State the power rating of resistors

subtopics.name: Ohm's law and Kirchhoff's laws
objectives: Apply Ohm's law and Kirchhoff's laws in calculations

subtopics.name: Power and energy
objectives: Solve problems on power and energy (treatment should include calculations)

subtopics.name: Fundamentals of magnetism
objectives: Identify the types of magnet
Describe magnetic properties of materials: magnetic flux, magnetic flux density, permeability, magnetomotive force and reluctance

subtopics.name: Concept of electric field
objectives: Describe the electric field and its properties: electric flux, electric flux density, electric field strength, permittivity and dielectric constant, potential gradient
Compare magnetic and electric circuits

subtopics.name: Capacitors
objectives: Identify the types of capacitor
Explain capacitance and dielectric
Relate the charge on a capacitor to the applied voltage
State applications of capacitors and voltage rating
Analyse series and parallel connection of capacitors
Calculate energy stored in a capacitor (E = 1/2 QV = 1/2 CV^2)

subtopics.name: Electromagnetic field
objectives: Describe the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor
State Fleming's Right Hand Rule
Calculate the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field (F = BIL sin theta)
State Lenz's law and Faraday's law
Calculate the e.m.f. induced in a coil (E = BLV sin theta); simple calculations on force and e.m.f. only

subtopics.name: Self and mutual induction
objectives: Explain self and mutual induction (qualitative treatment)
Calculate energy stored in a coil (E = 1/2 LI^2)
Describe applications of electromagnetism: electric bell, security alarm system, solenoid, loudspeaker, buzzer, moving-coil instruments etc.

subtopics.name: Moving-coil instrument
objectives: Describe the construction, advantages and disadvantages of the moving-coil instrument
Explain conversion of a moving-coil instrument to an ammeter and voltmeter
Calculate shunts and multipliers

subtopics.name: Moving-iron instrument
objectives: Describe the construction, principles of operation, advantages and disadvantages of the moving-iron instrument

subtopics.name: Digital instrument
objectives: Identify digital instruments (multimeter, voltmeter, ammeter etc.) and state their advantages and disadvantages

subtopics.name: Binary number
objectives: Convert decimal numbers to binary numbers and vice versa

subtopics.name: Logic gates
objectives: Describe series connection of switches (AND gate), parallel connection of switches (OR gate) and the inverter (NOT gate)
Draw truth tables for logic gates
Draw the general symbols for AND, OR, NOT, NAND and NOR gates
Write Boolean expressions

subtopics.name: Generation of e.m.f. in a single turn coil
objectives: Plot a labelled sinusoidal waveform for a complete cycle

subtopics.name: A.C. quantities
objectives: Define a.c. quantities: r.m.s., peak and average values, form factor, cycle, period and frequency

subtopics.name: RLC circuits
objectives: Solve problems involving RL, RC and RLC series circuits
State the conditions for resonance
Draw the phasor diagram of series resonance

subtopics.name: Types of transformer
objectives: Describe transformer construction
Classify transformers by construction (shell and core) and by function (current and voltage)

subtopics.name: Principles of operation of a transformer
objectives: Explain the operation and transformation ratio of a transformer

subtopics.name: Losses and temperature rise in transformers
objectives: Identify transformer losses (copper and iron)
Describe the effect of losses and temperature rise in a transformer (qualitative treatment only)

subtopics.name: Efficiency of transformers
objectives: Explain losses and efficiency of a transformer

subtopics.name: Cooling of transformers
objectives: State the methods of cooling and the need for cooling

subtopics.name: Power supply units
objectives: Describe power supply units: dry cell, solar cell, cadmium cell and accumulator
Draw the block diagram of a d.c. power supply and state the functions of its blocks

subtopics.name: Rectification
objectives: Explain half-wave and full-wave rectification
Explain filtration and stabilization

subtopics.name: A.C. motors (single phase)
objectives: Identify the types of single phase motor: split-phase, capacitor-start, capacitor-run
State applications of single-phase motors

subtopics.name: Alternators
objectives: Explain the principles of operation, parts and types of alternators
Relate speed, number of poles and frequency (f in Hz)

subtopics.name: A.C. motors (three phase)
objectives: Explain the principles of operation, parts, types and application of three-phase motors
State the methods of starting: direct-on-line, star delta and auto transformer

subtopics.name: D.C. generators
objectives: Explain the principles of operation, parts and methods of connecting field windings

subtopics.name: D.C. motors
objectives: Explain the principles of operation, parts, types (shunt, compound, series) and application of d.c. motors

subtopics.name: Generating station
objectives: State the methods of generating electrical power: diesel engine, steam engine, hydro-electric, nuclear, gas turbine

subtopics.name: Electrical installation
objectives: Identify the types of wiring: surface, conduit, trunking, ducting
Select materials, tools and accessories
Apply the IEE wiring regulations regarding domestic installation

subtopics.name: Wiring
objectives: Identify cables and accessories
Determine the current-carrying capacity of cable
Wire lighting and socket outlets and connect plugs
Carry out conduit, surface, trunking and ducting installations

subtopics.name: Protection
objectives: Identify protective devices
Describe fuses and circuit breakers
Explain discrimination of protective devices

subtopics.name: Earthing
objectives: State the reasons for earthing
Describe the methods of earthing
Explain earth loop impedance

subtopics.name: Maintenance, fault diagnosis and repairs
objectives: Identify the types of fault: short circuit, open circuit and earth leakage
Diagnose and repair faults in an installation and equipment such as fluorescent fitting, electric iron, electric fan, blender etc.

subtopics.name: Testing of an installation
objectives: Carry out continuity test, insulation resistance test, earth leakage test and polarity test

subtopics.name: General workshop safety
objectives: Apply electrical safety regulations

topics.name: Electricity Transmission and Distribution
topics.content: Transmission: layout diagram of a high voltage overhead transmission system; main components (towers, insulators and conductors) and their functions, without detailed treatment of components. Operating voltage levels for transmission lines (132 kV and 330 kV) and the need for a high voltage system should be emphasized. Distribution: layout diagram and main components of electricity distribution; functions of substation components (transformers, feeders etc.).

subtopics.name: Transmission
objectives: Draw the layout of a high voltage overhead transmission system
State the functions of towers, insulators and conductors
State the operating voltages of transmission lines (132 kV and 330 kV) and explain the need for high voltage

subtopics.name: Distribution of electricity
objectives: Draw the layout and identify the main components of electricity distribution
State the functions of substation components (transformers, feeders etc.)

topics.name: Maintenance and Repair of Various Electrical Appliances

subtopics.name: Maintenance
objectives: Identify the types of maintenance: predictive, preventive and corrective

subtopics.name: Maintenance and repair of electrical appliances
objectives: Identify common faults in electrical appliances (blender, electric iron, electric kettle, toaster, fluorescent lamps etc.) such as short circuit, open circuit and earth fault
